When the surface water temperature in the eastern Pacific Ocean becomes warmer than normal, it can disrupt the normal flow of ocean currents, which can have a ripple effect on the weather patterns around the world.
During an El Niño event, the warm water in the eastern Pacific Ocean can move towards the west, where it can cause changes in the weather patterns in the western Pacific. This can lead to changes in rainfall patterns, droughts, and floods in different parts of the world.
El Niño events can also have a significant impact on the global economy, as they can disrupt trade and transportation routes, and cause disruptions in food production and distribution.
